one_liner: GoHighLevel has a broad REST API (v2/v3) with OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens, but there is no free tier. Access needs a paid plan or the 14-day trial. An official MCP server is claimed but not confirmed by the pages.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 is for Marketplace and public apps. Private Integration Tokens are static bearer tokens created in Settings and remain valid until rotated. The vendor help center says both are available on all plans. Legacy v1 API keys are being phased out and are not counted.
access_notes: No free tier. API access comes with paid plans (Starter $97, Unlimited $297, Founder $497/month). A standard 14-day trial is available from a third-party source, so working credentials during the trial are plausible but not vendor-confirmed in these pages. Create Sub-Account and Enable SaaS need the Founder plan (formerly Agency Pro).
blocker_notes: A paid HighLevel subscription or the time-limited trial is needed for credentials. Some endpoints need the Founder plan. The MCP claim is not verifiable from the supplied pages: the MCP help-center page was not fetched, and the registry signal is empty. Composio lists only a 'HighLevel MCP' toolkit with API_KEY auth.

evidence.quote: Both OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across plans.
Remain valid until rotated or revoked
It comes with the paid plans
Sign up on GoHighLevel's own site and you get the standard 14 days, with no bootcamp.
Creating sub-accounts through the API requires the **Founder Plan ($497/month)**, formerly Agency Pro, which includes Advanced API Access.
HighLevel's own index lists 794 endpoints in 46 services for v3.
